sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Construct was expressed, purified, and used for cryo-EM structure determination, confirming membrane insertion and correct folding; no explicit signalling functional assay (e.g., cAMP or Ca2+ response) is reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: GPBAR1 has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–19 as the extracellular N-terminal domain and TM1 begins at residue 20, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag. The clip names only 'N-terminus' with no residue number, so the junction is topology-derived (insert_after_residue = 0, before residue 1 M). The 19-residue native extracellular segment provides ample buffer (>3 aa) between the tag and TM1. The construct was successfully used for cryo-EM, confirming surface expression and correct folding. Full-length membrane-anchored GPBAR1 construct used for cryo-EM structure determination; an exogenous HA signal peptide, FLAG epitope, 3C protease site, and BRIL thermostabilizer were fused at the N-terminus of GPBAR1 to facilitate expression and purification.

sources.claim: To facilitate protein expression and subsequent purification, a HA signal peptide followed by a FLAG epitope, a 3 C protease site, and thermostabilized apocytochrome b562RIL (BRIL) were added at the N-terminus of GPBAR1.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It supports a single N-terminal prepend site. No internal extracellular loop insertions are supported by the ledger. The BRIL fusion is a thermostabilizing domain rather than a short epitope tag, but the FLAG epitope within the same N-terminal cassette qualifies as the short tag. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions were reported in the ledger.
